attempts.summary: On node1, set /etc/security/pwquality.conf minlen=12 and minclass=3 (backed up original first). pam_pwquality was already wired into system-auth/password-auth as 'requisite', so no PAM changes were needed. Validated as the actual target user (not root, which bypasses pwquality) that short and low-complexity passwords are rejected and a 12+ char, 3-class password is accepted. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured healthy baseline (boot_id, config, PAM wiring), issued a non-blocking shutdown -r now, confirmed disconnection then reconnection, proved boot_id changed (e9250ad1... -> 2d4bc72a...) with uptime reset to 0, and re-verified the policy config and functional enforcement post-restart.
